feedback: This candidate maintains the proven geometry and sensor layout from iteration 1, which yielded strong performance with zero line loss events and low RMS error. The controller changes—reducing kp to 3.0 and increasing kd to 7—are consistent with the previous evaluator suggestion to reduce oscillations, supported by iteration 1's lower steering oscillation at kd=6 and kp=4. The base_speed increase to 1.7 aims to improve completion time, building on iteration 1's success at 1.6 speed. The switch to 'search_right' for line loss recovery is a reasonable test of alternative recovery behavior, though iteration 1's 'search_left' showed zero line loss events, so this change's benefit depends on future race data. If the next race shows reduced steering oscillation and no line loss events, consider further increasing base_speed up to 1.8 to improve completion time, as iteration 1's completion time was 2.48s at 1.6 speed. If steering oscillation remains high, try reducing kp further to around 2.5 and increasing kd slightly to 8 to enhance damping. If line loss events occur, evaluate whether 'search_right' or reverting to 'search_left' is more effective. Requested changes: 1) controller.kp to 2.5 to test reduced proportional gain for oscillation control (iteration 1 evidence); 2) controller.kd to 8 to test stronger damping (iteration 1 evidence); 3) controller.base_speed to 1.8 if completion time improves, to push speed further (iteration 1 evidence).
